text: You're on the last train home. The man next to you... hasn't breathed in minutes.
Then... his finger moves.
These are your next three days. And what kills you... won't be the zombies.
Suddenly, his head snaps up. His eyes are white.
Someone screams at the end of the car. And in a second, everyone runs.
But you? You can't move.
That's normal. In real disasters, almost 3 in 4 people just freeze.

text: The doors open. Run.
Outside, nothing but sirens. The roads are closed. Nobody answers your call.
One bite becomes two. Two become four. In a few days... the whole city.
In a zombie simulation by Cornell University, the cities fell first.
The safest place? Far away from people.
Day three. You're hiding in a grocery store. The water is almost gone.
Then... a knock.
Help me... I'm not bitten.
You open the door...
But here's the scary part: real zombies exist in nature.
A fungus gets inside an ant, takes control of its body, makes it climb a leaf... and grows out of its head.
And rabies? Victims turn aggressive, become afraid of water, and it spreads through bites.
So remember: what kills you isn't the zombie. It's the voice in your head saying, this isn't real.
